notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b, five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head 74112b4, uncommitted false, rc 0, model_id equal to the requested model, files [review.md] and reads []. Every assistant message in each transcript reports only the run's model; each transcript shows a Read of code-review-input.ex and a Write of review.md, no Skill call and no skill file read (no transcript contains the skill's text). Opus-1 also ran the original and its rewrite in a check_tmp folder inside its run folder, which it removed, and sonnet-1 edited its review three times. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex. result.json has no format_ok field, so format_ok comes from this grade's own check.

Rule list: the same 16 index rows as the 2026-10-31 grade. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes no rule in the list: it adds a `for` sentence to 'One expression per line, and tabular clauses', removes 'A `for` always takes `do ... end`' and its example from 'Use `do:` for a one-expression body...', changes references/macros.md and shortens an example under 'Use ETS for data many processes read' in references/processes.md. So no changed sentence decides a verdict, and all 16 rules are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it; a silent fix does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported, the improved code keeps it, or the code adds a new instance; a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the 120, while a fix naming `@max_age` does; a one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body or `case` clause is not nesting; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; `Map.get/2` on a struct breaks the required-keys rule; an assumed or companion changeset counts as a changeset, and hand parsing beside it is allowed; a `change/1,2` that validates nothing breaks the changeset rule. The two changed layout rules are outside the list and are checked only for other_violations.

Planted problems, mapped as in the 2026-10-31 grade: 21 problems from the case table's 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding counted apart from the magic 120 and the line 49 spawn apart from the closure copy. Counts: opus-1 15, haiku-1 12, haiku-2 12, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 13 (2026-10-31: 17, 12, 11, 15, 16). No run reports the line 12 pipe, the line 21 `&&`, the magic 18, the bare-struct insert as a validation problem or the closure copy. All five report the line 24 lookup-before-insert with the race: opus-1 (finding 3), sonnet-1 (finding 5) and sonnet-2 (finding 4) drop `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint(:email)`; haiku-1 (finding 7) and haiku-2 (finding 6) report it and keep it.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Bare-struct insert: opus-1's finding 3, sonnet-1's finding 5 and sonnet-2's finding 4 name a changeset or `unique_constraint` only as the fix for the race and do not mention validation, so they do not report it, as the 2026-10-23 sonnet-2 grade ('names a changeset only for `unique_constraint(:email)`') and the 2026-10-22-d sonnet-1 grade judged the same wording. All three go on to use `change/2`, so their changeset verdicts are violated either way. Opus-1 names nothing about input line 33, and its line 139 drops the changeset, so 'Match every expected shape...' is violated even though it fixes the identical errors, as for the 2026-10-22-c sonnet-2 run; its comment on line 138 explains the drop but is not a finding. Haiku-2's line 127 note says the insert errors stay collapsed and sits outside the findings, so it does not count for input line 33. Haiku-1's finding 3 ('A `nil` role also crashes here.') counts for the missing role, borderline, since it does not say the line is outside the `try`. Haiku-1's nesting counts through finding 4's 'chain the steps with `with`' and sonnet-1's through finding 3's 'use `with`', as 2026-10-31 counted those wordings; sonnet-2's finding 3 names no `with` and no nesting, so it misses it. Haiku-1's finding 4 and haiku-2's finding 3 treat the rescue only as hiding failures and do not count for the identical errors. Haiku-2's finding 8 counts for the dead `is_binary`, as haiku-1's finding of the same shape did in 2026-10-31. Sonnet-1's finding 8 counts for the overlap; sonnet-2's finding 9 ('clumsier than `Keyword.get`') does not, so its silent drop of `:silent` leaves the overlap unreported. Opus-1 reports the overlap (finding 13) and the `Mailer` problem (finding 12) but keeps both by its own statement, which counts them as reported and the 'applies every finding' check as missed. Opus-1's magic 120 counts through finding 4's `@max_age`; the other four propose `min(age, 120)`.

'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression' stays clean in all five. The one borderline case is haiku-2 lines 56-62, where `mix format` spreads `insert_user(email: email, age: age, role: role, nickname: params["nickname"] || email)` over seven lines inside a `with` clause. It is decided by 'what helps is finding the distinct conceptual steps inside it' and 'Length alone decides nothing': the call is one step, and 'Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call' keeps a trailing keyword list inline, one option per line. Binding the fallback, as opus-1 line 88 does, would read better, but the rule does not require it, so it is not counted, in line with the 2026-10-31 treatment of the formatter's own wrap.

False positives: sonnet-2's finding 9 calls line 27's operators clumsier than `Keyword.get` (borderline); it does not put `and` or `not` on a nil-able option, since the code drops `:silent`. Sonnet-1's finding 8 and opus-1's finding 13 treat line 27 only as overlapping options; the haikus do not discuss it. Must-not-report line 11: the why-comment is kept by opus-1 (line 103), sonnet-1 (line 65) and sonnet-2 (line 68), and both haikus drop it without a finding. Line 19: opus-1's finding 8 is about blank CSV cells, not the optional read or the fallback, so it is not counted, as before; this time its code replaces `||` with `parse_nickname/2` clauses (lines 127-128), and the fallback to the email stays. Every other run keeps `||`.

Rules outside the list, checked against their current text for other_violations. Naming bullet ('A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`'): haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 name such functions `fetch_*`; no run of this case in the 2026-10-23 or 2026-10-31 sweep used such a name. 'Use `do:`...' ('A `do:` body belongs on the head's line'): haiku-1 and haiku-2 lines 68-69 wrap a 96-character clause `mix format` would keep on one line; sonnet-1 lines 66-67 wrap a long pipeline body under a short guard; sonnet-1 lines 79-80 are 105 characters on one line with a long guard, the wrap the rule keeps, so they are not counted. The `->` rule: sonnet-2 lines 101-103 put a one-call `fn` below its head though the one-line form is 94 characters; the `Accounts.TaskSupervisor` forms in opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 would be 102 characters and are fine. Haiku-2's line 64 `{:ok, if(opts[:return_id], do: user.id, else: user)}` is graded under the return-shape rule and is not listed again. Directives are in order in every run, every `with` has two or more `<-` steps, and no multi-line map or struct is passed inline. No run validates its options, and only opus-1 documents them under '## Options'; earlier grades did not list that, so it is not listed.

Format check: the one elixir block in each review.md was extracted to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-b/code-review-baseline/baseline-<run>.ex. `mix format --check-formatted` (Elixir 1.20.3) exits 0 for all five; a misformatted control (bad.ex) exits 1.

Compile and no-options check: each module was run by drive/run.exs in the scratch folder, a copy of the 2026-10-31 harness, against real Ecto (Mix.install) with an `Accounts.User` schema (email, age, role as `Ecto.Enum` of :admin and :member, nickname), an `Accounts.Repo` whose `get_by/2` returns nil and whose `insert/1` applies a changeset's action or returns a struct as given, `Mailer` and `Accounts.Mailer` stubs and a real `Accounts.TaskSupervisor`. All five compile with no warnings. In all five, `import_user(%{"email" => "Ann@Example.com", "age" => "130", "role" => "member"})` with no options returns {:ok, user} with age 120 and a lowercased email and sends no mail, and `notify: true` delivers one email. Age 17 and a missing role return an error in all five. An unknown role "root" returns an error in four, but haiku-1's `String.to_existing_atom/1` accepts it and stores `:root`. Haiku-2's email reads 'Hi there' because `Map.get(user, :name)` is nil. The stub Repo has no database, so `unique_constraint/3` was not exercised.

Compared with the 2026-10-31 baseline per_rule, four of the 16 rows change, none because of a rule edit. 'Match every expected shape...': opus clean to violated (opus-1 no longer reports the dropped insert error). 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...': haiku violated to clean (both haikus now report the nesting through a `with` fix) and sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2 no longer reports it). 'Validate input with changesets': opus and sonnet clean to violated (opus-1 and both sonnets go back to a `change/2` that validates nothing, and no run reports the bare struct). Rules broken per run: opus-1 7, haiku-1 11, haiku-2 9, sonnet-1 5, sonnet-2 8 of 16 (2026-10-31: 5, 14, 10, 6, 4).
Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex.
